wstep: This card describes the NCHFP method for canning whole sweet or sour cherries in a boiling-water canner, here for sour cherries. [T:SLO-095]

akapity: Stem and wash the cherries; you may remove the pits. [T:ACI-180]
If you pit them, put them in water containing ascorbic acid so they do not darken at the stem end. [T:ACI-180]
If you leave the pits in, prick the skins on opposite sides with a clean needle so they do not split. [T:ACI-180]
Cherries may be canned in water, apple juice, white grape juice or syrup. [T:ACI-180]
Syrup helps keep the flavor, color and shape of the fruit, but it does not prevent spoilage. [T:ACI-067]
For a very light syrup (about 10% sugar) NCHFP uses 6 1/2 cups of water and 3/4 cup of sugar for a load of 9 pint jars, or 10 1/2 cups of water and 1 1/4 cups of sugar for 7 quart jars. [T:ACI-192]
Heat the water and sugar together and bring to a boil. [T:ACI-192]
Hot pack: in a large saucepan bring the drained cherries to a boil with 1/2 cup of water, juice or syrup for each quart of fruit. [T:ACI-181]
Fill the jars with the cherries and cooking liquid, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace. [T:ACI-181]
Raw pack: put 1/2 cup of hot water, juice or syrup into each jar and fill it with drained cherries, shaking them down gently as you fill. [T:ACI-182]
Add more hot liquid, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace. [T:ACI-182]
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m) process hot-packed pints for 15 minutes and quarts for 20, and raw-packed pints or quarts for 25 minutes. [T:ACI-070,ACI-176]
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased. [T:ACI-015]
At 1001–3000 ft (above 300 m up to 900 m): hot pack 20 minutes for pints and 25 for quarts, raw pack 30 minutes. [T:ACI-183,ACI-176]
At 3001–6000 ft (above 900 m up to 1800 m): hot pack 20 minutes for pints and 30 for quarts, raw pack 35 minutes. [T:ACI-184,ACI-176]
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m): hot pack 25 minutes for pints and 35 for quarts, raw pack 40 minutes. [T:ACI-185,ACI-176]
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m, 3000 ft becomes 900 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m. [T:ACI-176]
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage. [T:ACI-015]
NCHFP times are for US jar sizes: a pint holds about 473 ml and a quart about 946 ml. [T:ACI-174]
JarAtlas rule (NCHFP does not test metric jars): for a jar of up to 473 ml use the pint time, and for a larger jar of up to 946 ml, for example 0.5 l or 0.9 l, use the quart time. [T:ACI-175]
This NCHFP recipe gives no time for jars larger than a quart, such as 1 l, so use smaller jars. [T:ACI-175]
